question: On which day was Delhi declared captured by the British during the suppression of the Revolt of 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 21 July
30 August
21 September
30 June
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 21 September

Explanation:
During the Revolt of 1857, Delhi was recaptured by the British on 21 September 1857. The British forces, led by General Wilson, breached the city through the Kashmir Gate and other entry points. Before this, the rebels had taken control of Delhi and declared Bahadur Shah Zafar as their nominal leader. The fall of Delhi was a major setback for the revolt, as it was the center of Mughal authority. After the capture, Bahadur Shah Zafar was arrested and exiled, and the British government took direct control of Delhi. This event marked a turning point in the suppression of the revolt.

☛ Where was Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled after the capture → Rangoon (Yangon)
☛ Who was declared the leader of the 1857 revolt in Delhi → Bahadur Shah Zafar
☛ Who was the British Commander-in-Chief during the capture of Delhi → Colin Campbell

question: At which of the following places was the 'Servants of India Society' founded by Gopal Krishna Gokhale in 1905? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)

question: On which of the following days did the Congress Party make a public announcement, urging Indians to celebrate it as 'Independence Day'? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 26 January 1929
26 January 1928
26 January 1930
26 January 1932
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 26 January 1930

Explanation:
The Congress Party made a public announcement on 26 January 1930, urging Indians to celebrate it as 'Independence Day'. This declaration followed the Lahore Session of the Congress in December 1929, where the 'Purna Swaraj' resolution was passed under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru. On 26 January 1930, the first Independence Day was observed across India, with the tricolor flag hoisted publicly. This day later became significant as the date for the enforcement of the Indian Constitution on 26 January 1950. The 1930 event marked a major step in India's freedom struggle, symbolizing the demand for complete independence from British rule.

☛ Date of first Independence Day celebration → 26 January 1930

☛ Slogan for complete independence → 'Purna Swaraj'

question: Who among the following leaders strongly supported the idea of self-reliance and was an extremist? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Surendranath Banerjee
Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Dadabhai Naoroji
Feroz Shah Mehta
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak

Explanation:
Bal Gangadhar Tilak was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement who strongly supported the idea of self-reliance (Swadeshi) and was an extremist. He was known as 'Lokmanya' and gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'. Tilak promoted the Swadeshi movement and emphasized the boycott of foreign goods. He propagated nationalist ideas through the newspapers 'Kesari' and 'Maratha'. He was the main leader of the Garam Dal (Hot Faction) and his ideology gave a militant edge to the freedom struggle.

☛ What is Tilak's famous slogan? → Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it
☛ Which faction did Tilak belong to? → Garam Dal

question: Who mobilised the headmen and cultivators of chaurasee des, moving at night from village to village, urging people to rebel against the British during the Revolt of 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)

Shah Mal
Gonoo
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shah Mal

Explanation:
During the Revolt of 1857, Shah Mal mobilised the headmen and cultivators of Chaurasee Des (a region in present-day Bijnor district, Uttar Pradesh). He moved at night from village to village, urging people to rebel against the British. Shah Mal was a local leader who opposed the injustices and tax policies of the British Raj. He united the peasants and led them in rebellion against the British forces. His revolt was primarily concentrated in the districts of Bijnor, Moradabad, and Saharanpur. Shah Mal is remembered as a prominent peasant leader of the 1857 uprising.

question: When did the sepoys in the cantonment of Meerut break out in mutiny? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 8 May 1856
10 June 1858
10 July 1859
10 May 1857
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 10 May 1857

Explanation:
The sepoy mutiny in the cantonment of Meerut broke out on 10 May 1857. This event marked the beginning of the Indian Rebellion of 1857. The immediate cause was the introduction of greased cartridges allegedly made with cow and pig fat, which offended both Hindu and Muslim sepoys. The Meerut sepoys rebelled, marched to Delhi, and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as their leader. This incident sparked the rebellion across large parts of North India.

☛ Which animal fats were allegedly used in the cartridges? → Cow and pig fat
☛ Where did the Meerut sepoys go after the mutiny? → Delhi

question: All of the following were extremist leaders, EXCEPT _____. (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Aurobindo Ghosh
Bipin Chandra Pal
Surendranath Banerjee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Surendranath Banerjee

Explanation:
Surendranath Banerjee was a prominent leader of the moderate faction in the Indian national movement. He advocated for reforms through petitions and prayers against the British rule. In contrast, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Aurobindo Ghosh, and Bipin Chandra Pal were extremist leaders who emphasized Swaraj and direct action. Tilak gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.' Aurobindo Ghosh promoted revolutionary activities. Bipin Chandra Pal led the Swadeshi and boycott movement. Thus, Surendranath Banerjee was not an extremist but a moderate leader.

question: The Revolt of 1857 ended with the British victory in: (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 1860
1867
1858
1877
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1858

Explanation:
The Revolt of 1857, also known as India's First War of Independence, ended with a British victory in 1858. The revolt began in May 1857 at Meerut and spread across northern India. The British East India Company suppressed the uprising through intense military action by 1858. Following the revolt, the Government of India Act 1858 was passed, which abolished the Company's rule and transferred the administration of India directly to the British Crown. Key leaders of the revolt included Bahadur Shah Zafar, Rani Lakshmibai, and Nana Sahib. The event marked a turning point in Indian history, leading to the establishment of the British Raj.

question: Which of the following Governor Generals of British India abolished the Doctrine of Lapse? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following is NOT the social cause of the Revolt of 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following events shook the foundation of British rule in India and led to the end of the East India Company's rule? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Battel of Banaras
The 1857 Revolt
Battel of Plassey
Battel of Buxar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The 1857 Revolt

Explanation:
The 1857 Revolt was the most significant event that shook the foundation of British rule in India and led to the end of the East India Company's rule. Also known as the 'Sepoy Mutiny' or the 'First War of Indian Independence', this uprising forced the British Crown to take direct control of India through the Government of India Act 1858. The immediate cause of the revolt was the introduction of the Enfield rifle cartridges greased with animal fat, which offended both Hindu and Muslim sepoys. The revolt began in Meerut on May 10, 1857, and quickly spread to many parts of North and Central India. Although it failed due to lack of unity and better British military strength, it ended the Company's rule and led to the beginning of the British Raj.

question: The Revolt of 1857 symbolically ended with the fall of which major city? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Delhi

Calcutta
Madras
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Delhi

Explanation:
The Revolt of 1857, also known as India's First War of Independence, symbolically ended with the fall of Delhi. Delhi was the political and military center of the revolt, where Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed as the leader of the rebels. The British recaptured Delhi on 21 September 1857, after which Bahadur Shah Zafar was arrested. This event marked the symbolic end of the revolt, although fighting continued in other regions. The fall of Delhi was a major success for the British as it broke the morale of the rebels and signaled the return of Company rule. It also led to the abolition of the Mughal dynasty and the eventual transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown through the Government of India Act 1858.

1857 के विद्रोह के दौरान, ग्वालियर में ब्रिटिश प्रतिरोध का नेतृत्व ह्यू रोज ने किया था। वह ब्रिटिश सेना के एक प्रमुख अधिकारी थे और ग्वालियर अभियान में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई थी। ह्यू रोज ने 1858 में ग्वालियर पर ब्रिटिश नियंत्रण स्थापित करने के लिए रानी लक्ष्मीबाई और तात्या टोपे की संयुक्त सेनाओं का सामना किया। 17 जून 1858 को कोटा की सराय की लड़ाई में उन्होंने विद्रोहियों को हराया, जिसमें रानी लक्ष्मीबाई वीरगति को प्राप्त हुईं। बाद में, ह्यू रोज ने तात्या टोपे को भी परास्त किया और ग्वालियर में ब्रिटिश शासन को मजबूत किया। हेनरी लॉरेंस लखनऊ में, जॉन निकोलसन दिल्ली में, और विलियम टेलर मध्य भारत के अन्य हिस्सों में सक्रिय थे।
